deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no derivation. It is a heavily corrected draft of a letter in German, almost certainly to Barnaba Tortolini, editor of the Annali di Matematica pura ed applicata. A later hand has written upside down at the foot: 'Riemann Entwurf eines Briefes ... an Tortolini'. The letter accompanies or announces Riemann's memoir 'Ein Beitrag zu den Untersuchungen über die Bewegung eines gleichartigen flüssigen Ellipsoides' (Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 9, 1861). Its content, paragraph by paragraph:

(1) Since 'last Easter' Riemann has carried his hydrodynamic investigations further. He found a large variety of cases in which the shape and the rotational state of a homogeneous self-gravitating liquid mass remain constant. These are the steady ellipsoidal configurations, today called Riemann ellipsoids.

(2) Most of these steady states are unstable ('labil') and so cannot occur in nature.

(3) Remarkably, the familiar Maclaurin case also belongs to the unstable states once the ratio of the smaller axis to the other two passes a certain value. The Maclaurin case is a rotating ellipsoid of revolution, with a = b > c. Modern value: e ≈ 0.9529, i.e. c/a ≈ 0.303. Riemann adds that Laplace overlooked this, since Laplace had asserted the stability of these figures.

(4) A courtesy paragraph asks the editor to look over the memoir. It explains that on a subject whose main points were already exhausted, he refrains from a detailed exposition.

(5) He stresses that his memoir differs essentially from Brioschi's 'beautiful work', despite a first-glance resemblance:
- Brioschi pursued Dirichlet's decomposition of the motion into two motions. Dirichlet himself had found this decomposition useless for actually determining the motion.
- Riemann starts from a different decomposition of the motion into three motions. This lowers the order of the system of differential equations to be integrated by two units and simplifies the problem.
- In the published memoir the fluid motion is the superposition of a rigid rotation of the ellipsoid's principal axes and internal motions with uniform vorticity. The extra first integrals (circulation and vorticity conservation) give the order reduction.

(6) He has read with great interest a memoir in recent issues of the journal. It sets out the genetic connection of Jacobi's creations in this field and, he says, gives them a more rounded, more beautiful form.

(7) He hopes that the memoirs on elliptic functions announced in the journal will soon appear. These are plausibly Betti's 'La teorica delle funzioni ellittiche', Annali 1860–61, though this is my identification. The remaining lines are too faint to read.

Context: the previous page holds Riemann's calculations for a variational problem in g, h, k with g^2+h^2+k^2 = ω^2. This is possibly related to the ellipsoid dynamics or to a top-like problem. It is not continued here. The next page is unrelated lecture or teaching notes on functions of x+iy.
errors: No mathematical steps on the page to check.

The claim about Maclaurin instability is substantively correct: Maclaurin spheroids become dynamically unstable at e ≈ 0.9529 (Riemann 1861; confirmed by Chandrasekhar and Lebovitz). However, Riemann's general energy-based stability criterion in the 1861 memoir was later shown to be inadequate in other cases (Lebovitz 1966, Chandrasekhar). It is not an error on this page, merely context.

Wording issue: the transcription reads the axis ratio as 'übersteigt' (exceeds). Physically the instability sets in when the ratio of the smaller axis to the others falls below a value, or equivalently the eccentricity exceeds one. The verb is barely legible and may be different.

results.what: Existence of a large family of steady ellipsoidal configurations of a rotating homogeneous liquid mass with internal motions
Maclaurin spheroids become unstable beyond a critical flattening; Laplace overlooked this
results.modern_name: Dynamical (bar-mode) instability of Maclaurin spheroids at e ≈ 0.9529
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1861; modern treatment by Chandrasekhar and Lebovitz (1960s)

results.what: Decomposition of the motion into three motions, reducing the order of the ODE system by two, as opposed to the Dirichlet/Brioschi two-motion decomposition
results.modern_name: Riemann's formulation of the Dirichlet–Dedekind–Riemann ellipsoid problem (rotation plus uniform-vorticity internal motion; reduction via circulation/vorticity integrals)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a letter draft summarising Riemann's published 1861 memoir on liquid ellipsoids. Its claims (many steady states, most unstable, Maclaurin instability missed by Laplace, a three-motion decomposition reducing the order by two) are all in the published work and credited to him. It is of biographical interest only: it records correspondence with Tortolini and comments on Brioschi, Jacobi and Betti.

checkable.asserts: Maclaurin relation Omega^2/(pi*G*rho) as a function of eccentricity; it vanishes for the sphere
Axis ratio c/a ≈ 0.3033 at the onset of dynamical instability e ≈ 0.952887, the 'certain value' of the smaller-axis ratio in Riemann's letter
Omega^2 along the Maclaurin sequence is maximal at e ≈ 0.9300, a nearby but distinct landmark from the instability point 0.9529

transcription_corrections: Upside-down note in another hand: read as 'Riemann Entwurf eines Briefes ... an Tortolini'. It identifies the addressee as the editor of the Annali; 'Ihres Journals' is consistent with this.
The verb in 'einen gewissen Werth übersteigt' is uncertain; physically the smaller-axis ratio must fall below a critical value.
'von Laplace ... übersehen worden ist' is plausible and consistent with Riemann's published remark on Laplace.

The '... herausgegebene Abhandlung' on Jacobi's creations and the announced 'Abhandlungen über elliptische Functionen' are likely Annali articles of 1860–61 (possibly Betti's 'La teorica delle funzioni ellittiche'). This identification is mine and uncertain.
